'''Douglas A. Melton''' is an American medical researcher who was the [[Harvard University Professor|Xander University Professor]] at [[Harvard University]] and an investigator at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] until 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/douglas-melton | title=Douglas A. Melton, PhD &#124; Former Investigator Profile &#124; 1994-2022 }}</ref> Melton was a co-director of the Harvard Stem Cell Institute and was an original co-chairman (with David Scadden) of the Harvard University Department of Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology. Melton was involved in the founding of several biotech companies including [[Gilead Sciences]], Ontogeny (now Curis), iPierian (now True North Therapeutics {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629112516/https://www.bioverativ.com/newsroom/bioverativ-completes-acquisition-of-true-north-therapeutics.aspx |date=2017-06-29 }}), and Semma Therapeutics. Melton is a member of the [[National Academy of the Sciences]],<ref>[https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/douglas-a-melton-idfdxd/ Douglas A. Melton, Harvard University]</ref> the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and is a founding member of the [[International Society for Stem Cell Research]].<ref name=time>[[Michael J. Fox|Fox, Michael J.]] (May 3, 2007). [https://content.time.com/time/specials/2007/time100/article/0,28804,1595326_1595329_1616837,00.html "The 2007 Time 100: Douglas Melton"]. ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''.</ref>

After decades teaching at Harvard, he left in 2022 to work at [[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]] full-time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chasing a cure for Type 1 diabetes |first=Alice |last=Park |work=TIME |date=February 11, 2026 |url=https://time.com/collections/time100-health-2026/7362551/douglas-melton/ |access-date=July 16, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Melton grew up in [[Blue Island, Illinois]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=FitzPatrick |first=Lauren |title=Time Will Tell - Scientist from Blue Island honored by Time Magazine |journal=[[SouthtownStar]] |volume=37 |date=June 3, 2007 |page=a3}}</ref> and completed a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in biology at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1975.<ref name=cv>[http://www.consumerwatchdog.org/resources/meltoncv.PDF Doug Melton's Curriculum Vitae]</ref> He was awarded a [[Marshall Scholarship]] for study at the [[University of Cambridge]] where he received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in the history and philosophy of science in 1977 and a PhD under the supervision of [[John Gurdon]].<ref name=gurdon/><ref name=meltonphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Douglas|last=Melton |title=The expression of transfer RNA genes to other DNAs microinjected into Xenopus oocytes |publisher=University of Cambridge |date=1979 |url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.465534}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Melton's early work was in general developmental biology, identifying genes important for cell fate determination and body pattern. This led to the finding that the nervous system in [[vertebrate]]s is formed as a default when early embryonic cells do not receive inductive signals to become [[mesoderm]] or [[endoderm]].<ref>{{Cite Q|Q34415315|doi-access=free}}</ref> He also pioneered the technique of ''in vitro'' transcription with bacterial SP6 RNA polymerase.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q27861016}}</ref> This RNA transcription system is now widely used to make large amounts of messenger RNAs in vitro and is, for example, the basis for production of the COVID mRNA vaccines.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In the mid-1990s, work in his lab became centered on the development of the [[pancreas]] aiming to find new treatments for diabetes.

In 2001 when President [[George W. Bush]] cut federal funding of embryonic stem cell research, Melton used private donations to create 17 published<ref>{{Cite Q|Q29999326}}</ref><ref>[http://www.jove.com/index/details.stp?ID=574 Derivation of Human Embryonic Stem Cells by Immunosurgery]</ref> human [[stem cell line]]s and distributed them without charge to researchers around the world.

In August 2008, Melton's lab published successful [[in vivo]] [[reprogramming]] of adult mice [[exocrine pancreas|exocrine pancreatic]] cells into insulin secreting cells which closely resembled endogenous [[beta cells|islet beta cells]] of the pancreas in terms of their size, shape, ultrastructure, and essential marker genes.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q28292190}}</ref> Unlike producing beta cells from conventional [[embryonic stem cells]] or the more recently developed [[induced pluripotent stem cell]] (iPSC) technique, Melton's method involved [[transdifferentiation|direct cell reprogramming]] of an adult cell type (exocrine cell) into other adult cell type (beta cell) without reversion to a pluripotent stem cell state.

His current research interests include pancreatic developmental biology and the directed differentiation of human [[embryonic stem cell]]s, particularly in pertinence to [[type 1 diabetes]]. In 2014, he reported a method using human pluripotent stem cells to generate virtually unlimited quantities of functional insulin-producing beta cells that respond appropriately to a glucose challenge.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q28249536}}</ref>

In 2022, Melton left [[Harvard University]] and joined [[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]] full-time to create diabetes treatments.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-05 |title=Douglas Melton, noted stem cell researcher, leaves Harvard for Vertex to create diabetes treatments |url=https://www.statnews.com/2022/04/05/douglas-melton-noted-stem-cell-researcher-leaves-harvard-for-vertex-to-create-diabetes-treatments/ |access-date=2022-04-05 |website=STAT |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Melton was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1995. In 2007 and again in 2009, Melton was listed among the [[Time 100|''Time'' 100]] Most Influential People in the World.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q28304304}}</ref> In 2016, Melton was awarded the Ogawa-Yamanaka Prize in Stem Cell Biology.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://gladstone.org/about-us/news/2016-ogawa-yamanaka-stem-cell-prize-awarded-douglas-melton|title=2016 Ogawa-Yamanaka Stem Cell Prize Awarded to Douglas Melton|last=PhD|first=Dana G. Smith|date=2016-09-27|work=Gladstone Institutes|access-date=2017-06-29|language=en}}</ref> In 2023 he received the [[Abarca Prize]] for his advances towards a cure for diabetes.<ref>{{Cite press release |last=Prize |first=Abarca |title=PROF. DOUGLAS A. MELTON, WINNER OF THE III EDITION OF THE 'ABARCA PRIZE' FOR HIS DISRUPTIVE CURE OF TYPE 1 DIABETES, IS RECEIVED BY HIS MAJESTY THE KING OF SPAIN |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prof-douglas-a-melton-winner-of-the-iii-edition-of-the-abarca-prize-for-his-disruptive-cure-of-type-1-diabetes-is-received-by-his-majesty-the-king-of-spain-301969050.html |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref>
